subject: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff
body:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>, Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

Team,

Sharing v0.9 of the pilot threshold proposal for Optimize Guardrails gating. This is the set we’ll ship behind the pilot feature flag if we can get Applied ML + Product signoff by EOW.

Docs / artifacts:
- Confluence: Guardrails metric taxonomy + threshold definitions (updated today)
- Attachment: Guardrails_Thresholds_Pilot_v0.9.xlsx
- Attachment: Gating_Mode_Output_Spec_v0.3.pdf (matches what Olivia is implementing in eval-harness)

What I need from this group:
1) Sana/Selene/Karthik: thumbs-up on the statistical guardrails (sample size + CI rules) and metric cutoffs for pilot
2) Aditya: confirm the “block vs. warn” behavior per tier in pilot aligns with rollout plan
3) Priya: exec signoff that we’re comfortable piloting with these thresholds (knowing we’ll iterate)

Summary of proposal (pilot):
- Baseline is “current config” for the same (model version, prompt-set revision, suite) as the proposed change.
- We compute deltas + confidence intervals and apply per-metric thresholds.
- Default: any “hard” metric fail blocks apply (except where explicitly marked warn-only). Overrides require justification (pilot: internal only + a few design partners).

Key threshold rules (details in sheet):
A) Binary pass/fail metrics (e.g., tool-call JSON validity, schema conformance)
- Use Wilson interval @ 95% CI
- Minimum n=200 prompts per suite (pilot), unless suite tagged “expensive” then n=80
- Fail if lower bound of delta < -0.5pp for “hard” validity metrics

B) Rubric/graded metrics (task success / helpfulness rubric)
- Bootstrap CI @ 95% (10k resamples)
- Minimum n=120 prompts per suite (pilot)
- Fail if lower bound of delta < -0.03 (on 0-1 normalized rubric)

C) Safety/toxicity
- Warn-only for pilot unless exceed absolute threshold (toxicity > 0.5% absolute)

D) Factuality proxies
- Pilot is warn-only; hard gating comes later (we’re not confident in generality across workloads yet)

Concerns we still need to resolve:
- Multiple comparisons: do we Bonferroni/Benjamini-Hochberg in pilot or accept higher false positives?
- Correlated prompts: our prompt sets include variants; we’re treating them as independent right now.

If folks can reply with “Approved for pilot” / “Blockers” + any edits by Thu 3pm, I’ll roll this into the final Confluence threshold spec and we’ll mark PM-844 ready.

Thanks,
Jonas

—
Jonas Weber
Evals Program Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 11:07 AM PST
Subject: Re: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

Thanks Jonas.

I’m mostly aligned but a few statistical notes before we declare this “signed off”:

1) n=200 for Wilson is okay for validity-type metrics, but the -0.5pp delta might be too tight given we’ll see some suite-to-suite variance + occasional harness flake. I’d prefer:
- keep -0.5pp for “strict” (schema conformance, JSON validity)
- relax to -1.0pp for “soft validity” (e.g., tool selection correctness if grader-based)

2) For rubric metrics: bootstrap CI is fine, but we should explicitly require:
- fixed grader version (and include grader rev in gating output)
- rerun-once rule if fail is within an “ambiguity band” (e.g., CI lower bound between -0.03 and -0.06)

3) Multiple comparisons: I strongly recommend we DO NOT add BH/FDR in pilot. It will be hard to explain and will reduce trust when a clearly worse change “passes” due to correction. Instead:
- keep suite count small for pilot
- treat “hard” metrics as hard regardless

4) Correlated prompts: agree we’re ignoring this for pilot, but we should add a note that n is “effective sample size” risk, and we’ll audit prompt set construction.

If we incorporate (1) and (2), I’m good with “approved for pilot” from the stats side.

Sana

—
Sana Farid
Applied ML — Thresholds/Stats
Redwood Inference



From: Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 1:26 PM PST
Subject: Re: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

+1 to Sana’s points.

Two additional “practical” items from the guardrails side:

- We should classify metrics as:
  (a) hard block
  (b) warn + allow override
  (c) informational only
  and put that directly in the threshold schema so Product/Console doesn’t re-encode policy.

- For quantization specifically, I want at least one formatting/structure sentinel suite that is hard-block even if overall rubric looks flat. We have multiple historical cases where output is “roughly as good” but breaks callers (markdown tables drift, JSON keys missing). (See the examples in the quantization regression cases doc.)

If Jonas can reflect these in the Confluence spec + the sheet, I’m comfortable signing off for pilot.

Selene

—
Selene Huang
Quality Guardrails Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>, Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Jan 14, 2025 at 3:02 PM PST
Subject: Re: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

Adding one manager-y concern: operationally, we need a clear answer for “what happens when evals are flaky / time out.”

I know the enforcement is in control plane and there’s safe-degrade policy work happening, but the threshold spec should still include:
- if a suite returns < min_n due to errors/timeouts -> treat as FAIL (or “inconclusive”?)
- if a suite is inconclusive, does it block apply or can we accept with override?

I’m ok with starting conservative (block on inconclusive) for pilot, but we need to make sure Product is aligned because it will show up as “blocked” even if quality might be fine.

Otherwise, +1 to Sana/Selene edits.

Karthik

—
Karthik Iyer
Applied ML Manager
Redwood Inference



From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>, Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 9:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

This looks directionally right.

Product POV / rollout alignment:
- Pilot behavior: “soft block” with override for internal + 3 design partners; everyone else is observe-only.
- For design partners: if the result is “inconclusive” (timeout / <min_n), we should present as “Needs manual approval” and require override justification. That keeps us safe and avoids calling it a quality failure.
- Console copy: we need stable, simple buckets: PASS / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE. (We can expose metric detail in an expandable panel.)

Re: multiple comparisons: agree with Sana — keep it simple in pilot; we can revisit when we add more suites/metrics.

Jonas: can you update the spreadsheet + Confluence with:
- hard vs warn vs info classification
- explicit “inconclusive” policy
- quantization sentinel suite requirement

Once that’s in, I’m comfortable calling this “Product approved for pilot” and we can close PM-844.

Aditya

—
Aditya Rao
Product (Optimize) — DRI
Redwood Inference



From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>, Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Jan 15, 2025 at 2:44 PM PST
Subject: Re: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

Updated per feedback:

Changes made (v1.0):
- Split validity thresholds into Strict vs Soft:
  - Strict validity (JSON validity, schema conformance): fail if CI lower bound delta < -0.5pp
  - Soft validity (grader-based “correct tool selected”): fail if CI lower bound delta < -1.0pp

- Added “Outcome semantics” section:
  - PASS: all hard metrics pass AND min_n satisfied
  - FAIL: any hard metric fails
  - INCONCLUSIVE: any required suite has <min_n or harness error rate >2% (post-retry)

- Policy for INCONCLUSIVE (pilot):
  - internal + design partners: block unless override (shown as “Needs manual approval”)
  - everyone else: observe-only logging (no block)

- Added requirement that gating output includes:
  - prompt-set revision
  - grader version
  - harness version

- Quantization: added mandatory “format + structure sentinel” suite:
  - hard-block metrics: JSON validity (if route uses tool calling), schema conformance (if structured output), and “format drift” heuristics (we’re using the existing regex-based checks for pilot)

Links:
- Updated Confluence section is live (same page)
- Updated attachment: Guardrails_Thresholds_Pilot_v1.0.xlsx (replaces v0.9)

If Sana/Selene/Karthik are comfortable replying “Approved for pilot”, we just need Priya’s signoff and we can proceed.

Jonas



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Sana Farid <sana.farid@redwoodinference.com>, Selene Huang <selene.huang@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Jan 16, 2025 at 4:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Thresholds proposal for Optimize Guardrails pilot — review + signoff

Approved for pilot.

Conditions / expectations:
- We keep the pilot population small until we’ve observed 1–2 weeks of pass/fail/inconclusive rates and have confidence we aren’t generating a high false positive rate that blocks reasonable cost savings.
- Any override usage for design partners needs to be auditable (who/why) and summarized weekly to Aditya + me during the pilot.
- If the runner is unstable and “inconclusive” spikes, we pause expanding the pilot (don’t loosen thresholds as a first response).

Thanks for tightening the “inconclusive” semantics. Please make sure Support/CS gets the “Needs manual approval” wording ahead of time so we don’t surprise design partners.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
VP Platform (Exec Sponsor)
Redwood Inference
